summary: The rewrite's target and gate are sound, but sub-change (4) runs the first launch in a multiprocessing-spawn child process, and TASK.md says a submission that 'starts processes' is rejected (DECISIONS 2026-10-24 already struck cuobjdump for this reason). Re-mint with (4) replaced by an in-process guarded first launch, and keep (1)-(3) and (5) as they are.
justification: A: The target is real. In FINDINGS, FA3's cutlass device_kernel is 415.4 us (26.8%) on turn_1 full, 1620.2 us (32.8%) on turn_4 full, and 4467/8017 us (22.9%/36.6%) on first_turn full ctx32768/65536. REWRITE_READ #3 puts FA3 at about 1.6x its exp floor (250/1000/555/2770/4990 us). So a wgmma FP8 core has physical room: M2 (0.75x FA3) is still above the floor. The stage-1 fixes match what REWRITE_READ #3 asked for: the sm_90a build fix plus the FEAT_SM90_ALL guard, mma.sync deleted, exp offload at 0/8, and a hard cold-L2 CUDA-graph gate at <=0.92x. The gate is keyed only on config/shape fields (batch, q_len, page_table width; reference.py sizes page_table as longest+q_len, so ctx0/32768/65536 do differ in width). It is decided in prepare() on synthetic inputs, which is legal. Expected directions agree with TASK.md: full classes faster or flat by construction, sliding flat. The headline stake is small. FA3 on full layers is about 8.8% of the turn_1 load (16x415 of ~75 ms), about 11% of turn_4, and about 7.5% of first_turn. A routed class at the gate threshold therefore moves its load by only ~0.6-0.9%, inside the +-1.5% CI, so this stage must be read from the GATE log lines and the profile's top_kernels, not the headline (correct for kind: rewrite). Weakest link: per the hypothesis's own risk note, the wgmma core is non-persistent and non-warp-specialized, and was written without ever being compiled or run on the judge. FA3 is a warp-specialized ping-pong kernel with intra-warpgroup softmax/MMA overlap. A non-WS core that serializes QK wgmma, softmax and PV wgmma will probably land at 0.95-1.4x FA3, so the most likely outcome is M0 plus every class gated to FA3. That is still a useful measurement, because the per-class ratios set stage 2's design (WS/ping-pong). Secondary risks: prepare() time (about 40 s build, then the self-checks, then 5 classes x 2 kernels x >=20 cold-L2 graph replays, with ctx65536 first_turn ~8 ms each) has to stay well inside 300 s and the 15-minute run, given master's existing prepare cost. The synthetic gate inputs should use dist=soft per-batch length spread at turn_4 so split/causal balance matches the judge.
confounders: none material: all four landed hypotheses (stack-tonight-five-prefill, sglang-pipeline-parity, experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256, experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn) touch router/align/experts/silu-mul, which run after attention. Master's side stream starts after attn_boundary, so nothing overlaps the FA3 call. REWRITE_READ confirms master's attention code is unchanged.

sglang-pipeline-parity defines the incumbent FA3 call (paged page_size 1, scheduler_metadata None on prefill, FlashAttnFwdCombine). The new kernel and the gate must compare against exactly that call, including its combine, which the change already specifies.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change touches only the full-layer attention call, and the code it replaces is identical on master and on the old base. The hard gate makes each class's decision self-attributing: the log prints FA3 us, new us and the ratio per class, and the profile shows which kernel ran. The only internal sub-change worth isolating, exp offload, is already removed (0/8). No landed hypothesis shares this kernel's launch sequence, memory traffic or numerics, so an ab-revert or ab-tune would measure nothing new. For a rewrite, the next stage is the follow-up.
rules_flags: BLOCKING: sub-change (4) runs the first launch and self-check in a child process ('multiprocessing spawn'). TASK.md Rules: 'A submission is rejected if it ... starts processes'. This project already applied that rule in review (DECISIONS 2026-10-24, bf16-lossless-exp4-weight-stream-rewrite: 'drop cuobjdump ... it starts a process'). Fix: remove the child process. In its place: (a) keep the __CUDA_ARCH_FEAT_SM90_ALL guard with an error-word #else; (b) after load_inline, call cudaFuncGetAttributes on attn_fwd_kernel<0> and require binaryVersion == 90, which proves the sm_90a cubin loaded, else OFF; (c) do the first launch in-process on a tiny synthetic config, inside try/except followed by torch.cuda.synchronize(), and read the error word; (d) build with -lineinfo. Accept the remaining residual risk: an illegal instruction would fail the check, costing one check and not a wrong result.

LESSONS.md line 143 prescribes the same child-process remedy and should be amended. The queued sibling experts-cuda-wgmma-grouped-gemm-remeasure-sm90a has the identical 'multiprocessing spawn' step and needs the same fix before it runs.

Non-blocking: the gate must branch only on config/shape (batch, q_len, page_table.shape[1] bucket, page_size, window, kv_scale), never on seq_lens or cache_seqlens values. _attn_splits must also be shape-derived, because a value-derived split count would be branching on input values inside the graph.

Non-blocking: queries are FP8 E4M3, as in FA3 (allowed). P in FP8 for the PV wgmma matches FA3's FP8 path. The causal mask may skip fully-masked future tiles, which is causal attention and not block-skipping, but no tile of the past context may be skipped. Self-check (b) compares against FA3 at the error bounds, and must keep the outliers case.
open_questions: Does the user want to confirm with the organizers whether a multiprocessing child used only inside prepare() counts as 'starts processes'? Until confirmed, treat it as forbidden. Record it in PENDING_USER.md rather than blocking.

What is master's current prepare() wall time? The gate's 5 classes x 2 kernels x >=20 cold-L2 replays plus a ~40 s nvcc build must fit inside 300 s, alongside the queued CUDA expert rewrite if the two are ever stacked.

Does the ported wgmma core use a 128-row Q tile per warpgroup with K/V double-buffered via cp.async or TMA? If K/V loads are synchronous with the wgmma, the ratio will be ~1.3x+ and stage 2 must go warp-specialized. Read the GATE ratios with that in mind.
